info.title: freepik/ai-image-relight
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "freepik/ai-image-relight", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. `x-comfy-router-input-modalities` records the media kinds the model is documented to accept; the request schema is shared across sibling models and may admit media kinds this model ignores. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

example.prompt: warm golden-hour sunlight from the left

blacks.description: Adjust the level of black color in the image.

brightness.description: Adjust the level of brightness in the image.

contrast.description: Adjust the level of contrast in the image.

engine.description:
Engine preset for relighting:
- balanced: Well-rounded, general-purpose option
- cool: Brighter with cooler tones
- real: Aims to enhance photographic quality (Experimental)
- illusio: Optimized for illustrations and drawings
- fairy: Suited for fantasy-themed images
- colorful_anime: Ideal for anime, cartoons, and vibrant colors
- hard_transform: Significantly alters the original image
- softy: Slightly softer effect, suitable for graphic designs

fixed_generation.description: When enabled, using the same settings will consistently produce the same image.

saturation.description: Adjust the level of saturation in the image.

transfer_light_a.description: Adjusts the intensity of light transfer.

transfer_light_b.description: Also modifies light transfer intensity. Can be combined with transfer_light_a for varied effects.

whites.description: Adjust the level of white color in the image.

change_background.description: When enabled, changes the background based on prompt and/or reference image. Useful for product placement and portraits.

image.description: Base64 or URL of the image to do the relight

interpolate_from_original.description: When enabled, makes the final image interpolate from the original using the light transfer strength slider.

light_transfer_strength.description: Level of light transfer intensity. 0% keeps closest to original, 100% is maximum transfer.

preserve_details.description: Maintains texture and small details of the original image. Good for product photography, texts, etc.

prompt.description:
You can guide the generation process and influence the light transfer with a descriptive prompt.
IMPORTANT: You can emphasize specific aspects of the light in your prompt by using a number in parentheses, ranging from 1 to 1.4, like "(dark scene:1.3)".

style.description: Style preset for the relight operation.

transfer_light_from_lightmap.description: Base64 or URL of the lightmap for light transfer. Incompatible with 'transfer_light_from_reference_image'

transfer_light_from_reference_image.description: Base64 or URL of the reference image for light transfer. Incompatible with 'transfer_light_from_lightmap'

webhook_url.description: Optional callback URL that will receive asynchronous notifications whenever the task changes status.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

generated.description: The finished generation's image URLs. Present and non-empty on the document Router returns; this list IS the result. The links are Freepik's own and expire.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Freepik upscale, skin-enhance, relight and style-transfer models: the terminal Freepik task document, forwarded unchanged. All six ids are SUBMIT-AND-POLL - `routerresult/classification.go` records each `POST /proxy/freepik/v1/ai/...` submit as `ReturnModeSubmitPoll` - and Router polls on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is the finished task rather than the `{"data": {"task_id": ..., "status": "CREATED"}}` handle the underlying submit answers with.
ONE document describes all six because Freepik answers one. The upscaler, relight and style transfer each poll their own submit path and the three skin-enhancer tunings share a single status route, but every one of those routes declares the same task document, and the three tunings (`creative`, `faithful`, `flexible`) are three settings of one operation rather than three result shapes. Each id publishes its own `example` so the asset the page shows is the asset that page's model produces.
THE ASSET IS `data.generated`, a list of URL STRINGS pointing at the generated images - not objects with a URL inside, so there is no deeper field to key completion off. A `COMPLETED` task carrying an empty `generated` is a success that produced nothing, and through Router that case never reaches the caller as this document: Router answers it as a Comfy Router error instead, so a `200` here always carries at least one image URL. `data.task_id` is the handle the poll was addressed with and must never be read as an asset.
The URLs are Freepik's own delivery links and they EXPIRE. Router does not re-host these images onto Comfy storage, so what a caller receives is Freepik's short-lived URL rather than a Comfy one - download the asset rather than storing the link.
`data.status` is Freepik's own UPPERCASE vocabulary (`CREATED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`), compared without case folding. `COMPLETED` is the one terminal success and the only value this document can carry: `FAILED` and a budget-exhausted `CREATED`/`IN_PROGRESS` reach a Router caller as a Comfy Router error rather than as this body.
